extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news editors, and newsroom managers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for publishing AI-generated news content in online newsrooms, emphasizing clear disclosure, accurate bylines, human editorial oversight, and factual verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear disclosure of AI authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no clear disclosure that it was written by an AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should explicitly disclose when an article was written by AI rather than omitting disclosure or burying it; readers must be informed that content was produced by artificial intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline transparency and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The website was caught publishing articles produced by an AI under the byline 'CNET Money Staff' and it was only discovered after some users clicked the byline itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use generic staff bylines for AI-generated pieces. Byline pages and author attributions should accurately reflect authorship and make it easy for readers to learn how the piece was produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit labeling language
rubrics_metrics.description: The byline page didn’t make it completely clear either, saying that 'This article was generated using automation technology' rather than saying it was written by an AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clear, non-euphemistic wording (e.g., 'written by an AI' or 'generated by artificial intelligence') rather than vague phrases like 'automation technology' that can obscure the role of AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human editing and fact-checking prior to publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET said that they were still editing and fact-checking those articles with humans before publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming human editorial oversight, ensure and document that human editors actually review, edit, and verify AI-generated content before publication rather than treating the claim as a shield for errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure factual accuracy and correct errors
rubrics_metrics.description: An article highlighted factual errors found in those AI-produced articles, undermining the claim of human fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated content must be verified for factual accuracy pre-publication. If factual errors are found post-publication, promptly correct, annotate, or retract and review editorial processes to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about the scope of AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: All totaled, it appears CNET has published some 73 articles using their AI system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should be transparent about the scale and frequency of AI use (e.g., how many articles, which sections), so readers understand how widespread AI authorship is within the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and substantive response to criticism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlets should engage constructively with criticism about AI usage—investigate complaints, be transparent about findings, and take corrective action rather than dismissing concerns.
